channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Tobacco Regulation: Asia
item.description: Asia’s nicotine regulation is moving in many directions at once: tighter cigarette controls, new rules for vapes, disputes over pouches and continued pressure from illicit trade. That patchwork matters because adult smokers do not experience policy as a regional trend; they experience it as access, price, risk information and legal certainty. Regulation that ignores product differences can protect cigarettes by default. A stronger approach would recognise local realities while keeping the goal clear: less smoking, less combustion and fewer preventable harms. (Published on September 07, 2026bytobaccoinsider.com)

item.title: Laura Hunter’s Tobacco Defence Does Not Survive Scrutiny
item.description: Dismissing harm reduction as “tobacco defence” is an easy way to avoid the harder question: what actually helps smokers leave cigarettes behind? Industry scrutiny remains necessary, but it cannot replace evidence on combustion, switching and relative risk. A debate that treats every safer nicotine product as a corporate trick leaves no room for consumer experience or measurable reductions in harm. Public health should be able to challenge tobacco companies without dismissing the tools that may make cigarettes less dominant. (Published on September 07, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: The Three A's: Why Access Decides Who Quits Smoking, and Who Doesn't
item.description: Access can decide whether quitting smoking is realistic or only recommended. Safer nicotine alternatives need to be available, affordable and acceptable enough for adult smokers to actually use them. Sweden’s experience shows the importance of meeting people with practical options, not just warnings about harm. Public health progress depends on making the route away from combustion easier to take. (Published on September 07, 2026byquitlikesweden.org)
